summary:
Vault Violet fails the collision test. The dark violet #B688FE is ΔE00 1.8 from GXS Bank's lavender, 5.0 from PayID and 5.1 from Zip. The light violet #7A36D0 is ΔE00 2.7–3.1 from the violets of bunq, Starling, Klarna and Jar. Violet and indigo (OKLCH h≈270–300) is the most crowded band in all 8 markets.

I checked 135 sampled colours, 60 of them from payment or checkout brands. Only two hue families leave room for a vivid accent that reads on near-black and stays ΔE00 ≥15 from every payment brand: magenta-pink (h≈325–350) and citron (h≈108–122).

- **A "Fuchsia" (recommended):** #FF4FB2 dark, #8E567C light. 7.01:1 on black, 5.57:1 on white. Holds up best under colour-blindness simulation.
- **B "Orchid":** #FE74FD / #925882. More distance from brands, but under protanopia it looks almost the same as the status blue.
- **C "Citron":** #A3B30A / #707102. Farthest from all brands, but under red-green colour blindness it merges with the amber and green status colours.

Light-mode variants have to be muted (C≈0.09–0.12) to pass 4.5:1 on white.

Theme: follow the system setting by default on both platforms, design and test dark first, and keep light mode fully equal. Android gets an in-app Light/Dark/System default switch; iOS gets no in-app switch.

Most hex values are sampled from brand sites and logos, not official guideline documents. Web search was unavailable (shared limit used up), so I fetched known URLs directly.

findings.claim: The proposed Vault Violet collides with existing brands in both modes. The dark variant #B688FE is ΔE00 1.8 from GXS Bank lavender #AF89F4 (Singapore), 5.0 from PayID #9E8AEF and 5.1 from Zip #9D80FF (Australia). The light variant #7A36D0 is ΔE00 2.7 from bunq violet, 2.8 from Starling's legacy purple, 3.0 from Klarna's accent violet #7039E2, 3.1 from Jar #7029CC and 4.3 from Zelle.
findings.evidence: CIEDE2000 computed from sampled hex values. My code reproduces the brief's earlier checks: #7A36D0 vs Jar #7029CC = 3.05 and vs PhonePe #5F259F = 8.98.

findings.claim: OKLCH hue ≈270–300 (indigo to violet) is the most crowded band. At least 17 brand colours across all 8 markets sit there: Affirm #4A4AF4, Shop Pay #5433EB, Zelle #6D1ED4, Klarna accent #7039E2, PhonePe #5F259F, Jar #7029CC, Groww theme #5500EB, MobiKwik #0A4BFF, MobilePay #5A78FF, KOHO #892CFF, EQ Bank #513BFC, Zip #6542BE/#9D80FF, PayID #9E8AEF, Beem #3305B2, GXS #771FFF/#AF89F4, Wio #5700FF, Tamara #5721F4/#8D65FF and NatWest #5E10B1.
findings.evidence: Sampled from each brand's own site CSS tokens, meta theme-color or logo SVG fills, then converted to OKLCH.

findings.claim: I searched the in-gamut OKLCH space (2° hue steps) for accents with chroma ≥0.15 and ≥4.5:1 on both #000000 and #212225, at ΔE00 ≥15 from all 60 payment/checkout colours and from the status colours. Only two hue bands qualify: magenta-pink (h≈325–350; best clearance 15.5–16.7) and citron/olive-yellow (h≈108–122; best 18.1–18.8). Orange, amber, green, teal, cyan, blue and violet all max out below 15. Teal and cyan cannot reach chroma 0.15 at that lightness in sRGB at all.
findings.evidence: Per-hue profile in the spec. Examples of the best achievable clearance: h50 6.5 (UPI saffron), h150 6.5 (Careem), h230 2.1 (Paytm), h290 4.5 (Zip).

findings.claim: Candidate A 'Fuchsia', dark #FF4FB2 = oklch(70.0% 0.230 350.1). Contrast: 7.01:1 on #000000, 6.26 on #121212, 5.31 on #212225, 4.36 on #2E3135; a black label on it scores 7.01. Nearest payment brand: slice #D30AD7 at ΔE00 16.0 (Klarna pink 16.8, iDEAL 18.8). Nearest of any brand: bunq's rainbow magenta stop at 10.8. Nearest status colour: red at 24.7. Worst colour-blindness (CVD) case: 10.8 (tritan vs red).
findings.evidence: WCAG 2.2 contrast, CIEDE2000, and Machado 2009 simulation at severity 1.0.

findings.claim: Candidate A light partner #8E567C = oklch(52.9% 0.090 339.9). Contrast: 5.57:1 on #FFFFFF, 4.89 on #F0F0F3, 4.26 on #E0E1E6; a white label on it scores 5.57. Nearest payment brand: YouTrip #702D82 at ΔE00 15.0 (PayNow 15.3, iDEAL 15.4). Nearest status colour: 30.0. Worst CVD case: 22.0.
findings.evidence: Computed. This is the most saturated magenta-family light colour that clears 15 from all payment brands. More chroma collides with iDEAL, PayNow, slice or YouTrip.

findings.claim: Candidate B 'Orchid', dark #FE74FD = oklch(77.0% 0.230 327.8), 9.13:1 on black, 6.92 on #212225. Payment-brand clearance is 17.1 (Klarna pink) and any-brand clearance 14.2 (GXS lavender). But simulated protanopia maps it to #669FFF, which is ΔE00 2.0 from the simulated status blue. The same failure applies to Vault Violet (1.8).
findings.evidence: Machado 2009 protan matrix at severity 1.0, applied in linear RGB.

findings.claim: Candidate C 'Citron', dark #A3B30A = oklch(72.9% 0.165 116.1), 9.01:1 on black. Payment-brand clearance is 18.0 (Atome) and any-brand clearance 15.4 (KOHO lime). Its light partner #707102 is 5.18:1 on white and 21.9 from the nearest payment brand. However, simulated protanopia and deuteranopia put the dark variant 3.4–4.0 from status amber and 6.7–7.0 from status green, and it is only 18.1 from status yellow even with normal vision.

No light-mode colour in the magenta or citron families can be both saturated and ≥4.5:1 on white while staying ≥15 from payment brands. Light variants top out around chroma 0.09 (plum) to 0.12 (olive). All three light variants drop below 4.5:1 on the #E0E1E6 surface (4.26, 4.08, 3.97), though they stay above 3:1.
findings.evidence: Computed against the app's current theme surfaces in mobile/src/constants/theme.ts.

findings.claim: The platform guidance differs. Apple says people 'often choose Dark Mode as their default interface style' and 'expect all apps… to respect their preference', and advises 'Avoid offering an app-specific appearance setting.' Android recommends in-app Light, Dark and 'System default (the recommended default option)'.
findings.evidence: Text read from Apple's HIG JSON and from the Android developer documentation page.

findings.claim: NN/g (Kohler & Zhang, 27 Aug 2023; survey of 115 mobile users plus usability sessions) found roughly one third use dark mode, one third light, and one third a mix. Users think about dark mode at the operating-system level, and NN/g says to 'Mirror the device's operating system dark mode settings by default.' The earlier NN/g review (Budiu, 2020) found light mode gives better performance for most people with normal vision and advised against defaulting to dark, while still letting users choose.

Peer-reviewed results from 2022–2025 are mixed and depend on context. Light (positive) polarity improved cognitive scores (Gazit et al., Ergonomics 2025, n=173) and VR/MR reading (Luzsa & Mayr, Ergonomics 2025). Dark mode improved accuracy on medium-complexity dashboard tasks and lowered perceived workload (Ettling et al., ETRA 2025). Performance differences were individual and did not change with age (While & Sarvghad, IEEE VIS 2024, n=134).

Young-adult evidence leans towards preferring dark mode, but not towards performing better in it. Participants aged 20–30 (n=28) significantly preferred dark mode in a BBC News-style app (Clarkfeldt & Bjørner 2025). Sethi & Ziat (Ergonomics, 2022/23) found younger adults 'expressed more interest in negative polarity', yet that polarity raised their cognitive load in dim environments. No finance-app-specific study was found.

Brand colours need adjusting for dark backgrounds: bright colours shift darker, dark ones lighter, and chroma drops (Kim, Lee & Suk, PLoS ONE 2025). Under dark polarity, red text caused the most visual fatigue and yellow the least (Fan et al., Sensors 2024).

Cultural associations relevant to the candidates. India: saffron is sacred in Hinduism and politically tied to the BJP ('saffronisation'); pink signifies a 'welcome embrace' and is the primary colour of Telangana's TRS party. UAE: green stands for 'growth and prosperity' (UAE flag guideline) and is associated with Islam. Singapore (Chinese tradition): red means good fortune and is forbidden at funerals, white is the mourning colour, yellow is prestigious, and 'green hats' mean infidelity. Pink is read as feminine in 21st-century Western usage.
findings.evidence: These are mostly Wikipedia summaries (tertiary sources) citing government or other sources; parts of the articles are tagged as needing citations.

findings.claim: The colour maths was validated. My CIEDE2000 implementation matches all 34 of Sharma, Wu & Dalal's test pairs (maximum error 4.9e-5). The WCAG relative-luminance formula, including the 0.04045 threshold, was checked against the WCAG 2.2 text.
findings.evidence: Ran against ciede2000testdata.txt and compared with the WCAG 2.2 definitions.

# Vaultwise signature colour: collision map, candidates and theme default (2026-10-10)

## 0. How the numbers were made

### Data collection
- **Brands covered:** 135 brand-colour rows (about 120 brands) across US, UK, euro area (EU), India (IN), Singapore (SG), Canada (CA), Australia (AU) and UAE (AE). Each market has 13–20 distinct brands.
- **No official hex for most brands.** Web search was unavailable (shared limit of 200 calls used up), so no brand-guideline or press-kit PDFs could be found. Every value except the Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons is **sampled**. The method column says how:
  - `CSS`: a CSS custom property or dominant hex served by the brand's own site on 2026-10-10.
  - `META`: the site's `<meta name="theme-color">`.
  - `SVG`: a fill in the logo SVG (Wikimedia Commons or English Wikipedia file pages, or the brand's own inline SVG or favicon).
  - `PNG`: the dominant logo pixel.
  - `DOC`: platform documentation. Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons are documented as black or white styles only.
- **Two tiers:**
  - `pay` (hard constraint, ΔE00 ≥ 15): wallets, P2P, payment rails, payment and checkout buttons, BNPL, UPI apps (including slice), and Jar as the direct savings competitor. 60 colours.
  - `ctx` (reported only): banks, neobanks and investing apps.

### Colour maths
Own Python implementation:
- **Lab:** sRGB, then linear (IEC 61966-2-1), then XYZ D65, then CIELAB (D65, 2°).
- **ΔE00:** CIEDE2000 with kL = kC = kH = 1, validated on Sharma's 34 test pairs (maximum error 4.9e-5).
- **OKLCH:** Ottosson's OKLab matrices.
- **Contrast:** WCAG 2.2, (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05), with relative luminance R,G,B ≤ 0.04045 → /12.92. Colours are treated as opaque sRGB.
- **Colour-blindness simulation (CVD):** Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009) matrices at severity 1.0 (full dichromacy), applied in linear RGB. "CVD ΔE" is ΔE00 between the simulated candidate and the simulated status colour.

### Status colours (proxies)
Vaultwise has not defined its status hexes, so Apple's system colours (HIG, June 2025 values) stand in:

| Status | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| green | #34C759 | #30D158 |
| amber (orange) | #FF8D28 | #FF9230 |
| amber (yellow) | #FFCC00 | #FFD600 |
| red | #FF383C | #FF4245 |
| blue | #0088FF | #0091FF |

### Surfaces (from `mobile/src/constants/theme.ts`)
- **Dark:** #000000, #212225 (element), #2E3135 (selected). #121212 also tested.
- **Light:** #FFFFFF, #F0F0F3, #E0E1E6.

### Search grid
OKLCH hue 0–358 in 2° steps, L 0.30–0.95 in 0.01 steps, C in 0.01 steps (0.005 in focused scans), sRGB gamut only.
- **Dark variant:** C ≥ 0.15 and ≥ 4.5:1 on both #000000 and #212225.
- **Light variant:** C ≥ 0.08 and ≥ 4.5:1 on both #FFFFFF and #F0F0F3.
- **Both:** ΔE00 ≥ 15 from every `pay` colour and every status colour.

## 5. Theme default

**Recommendation: follow the system appearance by default on both platforms.** Design and test dark first, and keep light mode fully equal.

### Platform rules
- **Android:** offer an in-app Light / Dark / System default choice, with System default preselected ([Android docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/theming/darktheme)).
- **iOS:** no in-app appearance switch. Apple: "Avoid offering an app-specific appearance setting" ([Apple HIG, Dark Mode](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode)).
- **Pay with Vaultwise button:** offer both a dark and a light style and choose whichever contrasts with the merchant page. Apple's guidance pairs black buttons with light backgrounds and white buttons with dark ones ([Apple Pay HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pay)); Google's says "Use dark buttons on light backgrounds… light buttons on dark or colorful backgrounds" ([Google Pay brand guidelines](https://developers.google.com/pay/api/web/guides/brand-guidelines)).

### Why
1. Apple says people "often choose Dark Mode as their default" and "expect all apps… to respect their preference" (HIG).
2. NN/g (2023; survey of 115) found about a third each use dark, light, or both, and that users think about appearance at the OS level. NN/g says to "Mirror the device's operating system dark mode settings by default" ([NN/g 2023](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode-users-issues/)).
3. Reading performance generally favours light mode for people with normal vision ([NN/g 2020](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode/); [Gazit et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1080/00140139.2025.2483451); [Luzsa & Mayr 2025](https://doi.org/10.1080/00140139.2025.2457470)). So forcing dark would cost readability on statements and amounts.
4. Young adults lean towards dark: [Clarkfeldt & Bjørner 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3803722.3803727) (ages 20–30, n=28) and [Sethi & Ziat 2022/23](https://doi.org/10.1080/00140139.2022.2160879). Dashboards can benefit too ([Ettling et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3715669.3725879)). That supports investing in dark mode, not making it the default.
5. Which polarity helps more varies by individual ([While & Sarvghad 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10841)), so both themes need to be first-class.
6. In dark mode, avoid long runs of red text ([Fan et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.3390/s24113516)) and use the adjusted dark variant of the brand colour ([Kim, Lee & Suk 2025](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0339392)).

**Documented (sourced or computed):**

- The platform guidance quotes.

- The cultural meanings, as given in the cited (tertiary) pages.
- "About 1 in 12 men have color vision deficiency" ([NEI](https://www.nei.nih.gov/learn-about-eye-health/eye-conditions-and-diseases/color-blindness)).

**Inference (mine):**
- That a sampled UI token is a brand's signature colour.
- The tier split: banks and neobanks were treated as context only, and Jar and slice were put in the payment tier.
- Using Apple system colours as Vaultwise's status colours.
- Ranking A above B and C.
- "Design dark first".
- The checkout-button pairing advice.
- How gender and culture affect reading of the candidates.
- Treating ΔE00 15 as meaningful for large differences. CIEDE2000 was designed for small differences, so treat values above about 10 as ordinal.
- Display P3 rendering was ignored.
